subject: Why does this code call function even when I haven't clicked the button?

messages.author: b3ce55cdeeae67fd
messages.subject: Why does this code call function even when I haven't clicked the button?
parts:
Following this SO post (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/25218848/execute-a-function-in-background-when-clicking-a-button-with-no-output-being-cha), I tried to code a button that calls a function only when the button is clicked:



      observe({
        if(input$samp > 0) {
          fullTimeInfo(input$term1, input$term2)
          output$compare <- renderPlot({
            fullTimeInfo()
          }) 
        }
      })


However, I can tell from print statements that the function is being called a second time after I click the button a single time. Why is this and how can I stop it? It's causing errors that interrupt the first execution of fullTimeInfo(). Thanks for any suggestions.

messages.subject: Re: Why does this code call function even when I haven't clicked the button?
parts:
p.s. Even when the function I am calling is quite simple (so can't be calling itself or be called from somewhere else in file), the function is executing twice. For example, here is my entire .R file included in server.R:

require(ggplot2)
require(lubridate)
require(plyr)
require(stringr)
require(jsonlite)
require(gridExtra)
require(httr)
options(warn=-1)


fullTimeInfo <- function(firstTerm, secondTerm, years = 10, start = 1905, end = 2015){
  cat("CALLING FIRST TIME INFO")
  
}

When I click the button in the server.R code listed above and click just one time, I see "CALLING FIRST TIME INFO" twice.

messages.subject: Re: Why does this code call function even when I haven't clicked the button?
parts: You probably shouldn't be assigning an output value in the observer. I think it's probably executing fullTimeInfo() once when the observer is triggered, and then one more time when the new renderPlot() is called.

observe({
        if(input$samp > 0) {
          fullTimeInfo(input$term1, input$term2)
          output$compare <- renderPlot({
            fullTimeInfo()
          }) 
        }
      })
I suggest pulling the renderPlot() outside of the observe() if possible.
